correct_completion: the students fell asleep on the bus.
full_sentence: Exhausted after the long hike, the students fell asleep on the bus.
acceptable_variants: the students dozed off on the bus.
the students were soon asleep on the bus.

options.text: the trail was closed the next day.
options.why_wrong: A trail cannot feel exhausted. In a participle clause, the subject of the main clause must be the one who feels or does the action in the participle phrase.

options.text: the students will fall asleep on the bus tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future time 'tomorrow' conflicts with 'exhausted after the long hike', which describes a completed event.

options.text: the students fall asleep on the bus every day.
options.why_wrong: The habitual present describes a routine, but the participle clause describes a single past event.

options.text: the students fell asleep on the bus.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a shared subject
explanation: The participle clause 'Exhausted after the long hike' must describe the subject of the main clause, so only the students can be exhausted. The main clause must also use a past tense to match the completed hike. Ukrainian speakers often prefer a full clause with 'because' or 'after', but English participle clauses are shorter and must share the subject of the main clause.
